chapter: Reels 1-2: Roy Brown, clubs and Sam Cooke
title: New Orleans club work, then joining Sam Cooke in 1960
summary: Mid-1950s clubs and balls in New Orleans, nine jobs a week, then the call to join Sam Cooke in 1960 and staying until Cooke's death.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes, mid fifties, early sixties. Uh, cause uh, I ended up in late, late uh, sixties. They all had Masons. Uh, I played like that, the Haven, uh, on, uh, North Clavin Street. Uh, well, yeah. Like I said, there were quite a few places that you could play. Big time, Crip, Jackson and La Salle, you know. Seals, Barb. We had a lot about, uh, the Forest Inn, first in Magnolia. This would be like Thursday nights. We had packed houses, Tuesday nights at these places. People was coming out to support a lot of music. Uh-huh. You know. And, uh, none of the sudden, jazz. We were playing jazz, but, uh, it just, it just good to see people out. Like I said, they didn't have no special night. Everybody would say, where are you playing today? I'm over here, this place. And then, uh, like I said, we used a variety of guys. You know, at the time I was the band leader. Sometime Ray Tyler would be the band leader. Chuck Beatty. We, another place we used to play all the time is Joy Tavern back in. Right. Good job. Yeah. As a matter of fact, that's where I was playing, uh, in 60, 1960, I left. I got a call for Sam, Sam Cook. Uh-huh. At Drees Mohammed, which is Leo Morris. Uh-huh. Was the first drummer with Sam, but he stayed about a month and he left. And he recommended me and they called New Orleans. Uh-huh. I was working at Joy Tavern at the time. So, in 19, at the beginning of 60. And I left New Orleans and I joined Sam. Uh-huh. And I stayed with him until he, tragic in his life, he got killed. Uh-huh. Uh, then I came back to New Orleans after he, well, they tried to get me to stay in Los Angeles. I said, no, come back home.
